title: Drills
summary: Runs of exercises over a lesson's own items, graded by the share answered right.
description: A drill practises a handful of words, sentences or a dialogue. Its exercises are built fresh each time from the items and their history, which decides how hard each one is.

stories.want: each word to get harder to answer as I get better at it

stories.as: a learner typing on a phone
stories.want: a slip of one letter treated as nearly right
stories.soThat: I am graded on my Polish, not my thumbs

requirements.text: A word never answered is shown on a card that is only read and then asked by multiple choice; one answered before is asked by multiple choice; one answered right on three different days in a row has to be typed.
Typed answers ignore case, punctuation and spacing, and accept Polish letters typed without their marks.
A typed answer one letter off a word of four letters or more is almost right.
A dictation or spoken sentence of three words or more with one word wrong is almost right.
An almost-right answer is logged as a mistake, earns half the XP, counts as half right in the drill's score, and brings the item back sooner instead of starting its reviews over.
A drill passes at `drill.pass-share` right; a drill of three to six scored cards also passes with a single miss, or two almost-right answers.
A drill with `drill.partial-share` or more right that does not pass is a partial; less is a fail.
An ace in a drill is a pass with every scored card fully right.

history.text: An ace in a drill is a pass with no almost-right answers and at least 95% of the scored cards fully right.
history.reason: The owner decided an ace means every answer right: at 95%, a long drill could have a miss and still be an ace.

requirements.text: Cards that are only read (a new word, a dialogue to read, a story panel) are not scored, and a drill with nothing scored is not graded.
A sentence whose words change their ending is built from tiles in dictionary form, and the learner picks the ending on each tile; a sentence without stored endings is built by plain ordering.
A wrong answer on a word shows example sentences for it: made once by a model and kept, or, without a key, taken from the learner's own courses.
After a word or sentence card is answered, the learner can talk about it with the tutor straight from the exercise; that chat has its own model setting and otherwise uses the tutor's model.
Each word's and sentence's review interval grows with right answers on different days, to at most `review.max-interval`; an item counts once a day.
A drawing that was not finished when the app closed is resumed the next time it starts, by the device that started it.
A scene or story whose drawing failed says so on its page and can be tried again; a picture lesson offers to draw the pictures still missing.

values.description: The share of a drill answered right that passes it.
The share that is a partial.
The longest a word or sentence waits for its next review.
